name: Open files and the seventh rank
goal: You can put a rook on an open file, put your second rook on the same file, and use a rook on the seventh rank to attack pawns and trap the king.
intro: An open file is a column of the board with no pawns on it. A rook on an open file can travel all the way into the opponent's position, so the first rook to get there owns it, and two rooks on the same file are stronger still. The best place to arrive is the seventh rank, the opponent's second row: a rook there attacks pawns that are hard to defend and keeps the enemy king shut in on its back rank, the row it started on.

parts.title: A file with no pawns
parts.keyIdea: Put a rook on the open file before your opponent does, then double your rooks: put the second rook on the same file.
parts.text: From a game played on Lichess. You are White, and both sides still have their rooks. Look for a file with no pawns on it, and ask which rook can get there first.
parts.line: Rac1 Rd7 Rc3 a6 Rec1 b5 Rc6

notes.text: The c-file has no pawns on it, so a rook on c1 looks all the way up to c8. Your rook on a1 was doing nothing; now it holds the file before Black's rook on d8 can get to c8.
The rook moves up to c3 to make room for the other one. From c3 it still holds the file, and your rook on e1 can now come to c1 behind it.
Two rooks on one open file back each other up. They are ready to go into Black's position as soon as a square on the c-file is safe to land on.

Black's pawn move to b5 emptied b6, so a rook on c6 now attacks the pawn on a6. Your front rook goes in, and the rook behind it guards it, so Black's queen cannot take it without losing the queen for a rook.

parts.title: A rook on the open d-file
parts.keyIdea: Use the open file to reach the seventh rank, where enemy pawns and pieces are attacked from the side.
parts.text: From a game played on Lichess. You are White, and your rook on d1 already stands on the open d-file. Black's bishop has just gone to b7. Where can the rook do the most damage?

notes.text: The rook runs up the open file to d7, on Black's second rank. From there it attacks both black bishops, on b7 and e7, and neither of them is defended. Black cannot save both.
Black guarded the bishop on e7 with the rook, so your rook takes the other one. You have won a piece, and your rook is still on the seventh rank.
The rook stays on the seventh rank: from c7 it attacks the pawns on c6 and a7. Bringing your other rook to the open d-file with Rd1 was also good.

parts.title: The second rook
parts.keyIdea: Two rooks on the seventh rank trap the king on its back rank and sweep up the pawns there.
parts.text: From a game played on Lichess. You are White, and your rook on b7 is already on the seventh rank. Black's rook has just gone to d2. What can your second rook do?
parts.line: Ree7 f5 Rf7+ Kg8 Rxg7+ Kh8 Rxh7+

notes.text: The second rook joins the first on the seventh rank. Now the pawn on f7 is attacked, Black's king is stuck on the back rank, and Black's rook on d2 is far away from its king.
Black moved the f-pawn away, so your rook checks from f7. The king can only go to e8 or g8.
The rook takes the g-pawn with check. Your two rooks guard each other along the seventh rank.
The rook takes the h-pawn, again with check. In a few moves the two rooks have won two pawns, and the king still cannot leave the back rank.
